Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Serialization — Serialization Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C001 · Latest development: C006 Definition and mechanism Serialization maps semantic fields to a specified byte sequence; decoding validates and reconstructs them. Width, order, version, bounds, and padding policy belong to that contract. A U8/U32-LE/U64-LE header occupies 13 bytes at offsets 0/1/5, independently of a native record’s possible 16-byte ABI layout. Packing removes some holes, not host dependencies. Publication and durability are subsequent operations. M004 extension: a binary32 representation word such as 3F800000 can be serialized as little-endian bytes 00 00 80 3F. Raw-bit preservation retains signed-zero and NaN-payload differences; canonicalization deliberately merges them. Numeric equality does not imply byte identity. This is a format policy, not permission to change existing files. M006 adds explicit schema/version/identity contracts, overflow-safe dimensions and resource limits, raw-word payload preservation, integrity coverage and a complete 52-byte demonstration. A native scalar writer is not automatically cross-endian stable. Prerequisites
Interpretation contract — Representation, type, and lifetime must identify what object exists. Fixed-width integer types — The representation width fixes byte count and valid shift range. Endianness — Byte order tells how digit significance maps to sequence positions.
Used by
Binary format contracts — uses this mechanism to define its representation, error or validation contract. Checksums CRCs and hashes — uses this mechanism to define its representation, error or validation contract. Floating-point canonicalization — uses serialization to establish this mechanism’s representation or policy. Atomic publication and durability — uses this mechanism as stated in its prerequisites.
Recall and next depth Explain why packed/native memory dumps do not establish a portable schema. Pending: Version migration, malformed-input protocols, other floating formats and cross-platform special-value transport. Source and navigation Narrative development C004 representation policy C003 teaching chapter · Part definitions · Dependency Map. Open Serialization in Volume 1

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Big endian — Big endian Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C003 Definition and mechanism The lowest address holds the most-significant octet. For 0x12345678, offsets 0–3 hold 12/34/56/78. A decoder repeatedly multiplies its prefix by 256 and adds the next octet. Integer value is independent of host order. Prerequisites
Endianness — Byte order tells how digit significance maps to sequence positions. Positional notation — Base-256 weighted digits give the codec’s numeric meaning.
Used by Update downstream uses when later chunks build on this concept. Recall and next depth Derive the base-256 prefix recurrence. Pending: Protocol-specific formats and endian-aware tooling. Source and navigation C003 teaching chapter · Part definitions · Dependency Map Reconstruction depth Big-endian byte order stores the most-significant byte of a multibyte integer at the lowest address. For the 32-bit value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mn>0</mn> <mi>x</mi> <mn>12345678</mn> <mo>,</mo> </math> the four bytes in increasing address order are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mn>12</mn> <mstyle scriptlevel="0"> <mspace width="0.278em" /> </mstyle> <mn>34</mn> <mstyle scriptlevel="0"> <mspace width="0.278em" /> </mstyle> <mn>56</mn> <mstyle scriptlevel="0"> <mspace width="0.278em" /> </mstyle> <mn>78.</mn> </math> Endianness describes byte ordering, not bit ordering inside a byte and not the abstract value of the integer. Arithmetic on a correctly loaded integer is independent of whether its bytes arrived in big- or little-endian form. The engineering boundary is serialization. A file or network protocol must declare byte order explicitly, because dumping a host struct makes the external format depend on machine layout, padding and host endianness. Network protocols traditionally use big-endian network byte order, but a custom format may choose either convention as long as decoding is explicit. A reliable parser reads bytes, validates length, reconstructs the integer with shifts or standardized byte-swap facilities, and tests known byte sequences. The failure to avoid is double-swapping: once bytes have been converted into host numeric value, downstream code should not keep carrying an ambiguous network-order integer type unless the API makes that distinction explicit.. Open Big endian in Volume 1

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Worked Traces — Worked Traces Phase 9-10 worked-trace navigation The full numerical traces remain in the continuous volumes; this page does not duplicate their calculations: Phase 9 Jacobian trace · Phase 9 integral and quadrature traces · Phase 9 oscillator and stability traces · Phase 9 optimization traces · Phase 10 outcomes and Bayes trace · Phase 10 Monte Carlo trace · Phase 10 online statistics · Phase 10 uncertainty and error metrics Phase 8 - From constraints to a stable SVD contract Follow one small rank-deficient fit through its geometry, answer, and checks. This supplements the Phase 8 story. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">[</mo> <mtable columnspacing="1em" rowspacing="4pt"> <mtr> <mtd> <mn>3</mn> </mtd> <mtd> <mn>0</mn> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd> <mn>0</mn> </mtd> <mtd> <mn>0</mn> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> <mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">]</mo> </mrow> <mo>,</mo> <mstyle scriptlevel="0"> <mspace width="2em" /> </mstyle> <mi>b</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">[</mo> <mtable columnspacing="1em" rowspacing="4pt"> <mtr> <mtd> <mn>6</mn> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd> <mn>5</mn> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> <mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">]</mo> </mrow> <mo>.</mo> </math> The first row observes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> </math> with gain three. The second row has zero coefficients, so it cannot produce the requested measurement five. The rank is one, the column space is the horizontal axis, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>b</mi> </math> lies outside it. The null space is the vertical axis: changing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </math> is invisible to the map. The SVD is already diagonal: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>U</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>V</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>I</mi> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>A</mi> </math>. The pseudoinverse is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Therefore <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> </msup> <mi>b</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Every <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> has the same residual <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>t</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> is its minimum-norm choice. This trace separately answers consistency, rank, nullity, residual, and the pseudoinverse policy. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>k</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> truncation, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Here the input already has rank one, so the approximation is exact. If instead <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, then keeping only the first singular direction gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, spectral error <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>2</mn> </math>, and Frobenius error <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>2</mn> </math>. The norm names state which reconstruction discrepancy is being reported. Now use centered planar samples <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Their sample covariance with divisor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>N</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. The first component follows the horizontal line; the zero second eigenvalue says the observed samples have no vertical spread. Add small measurement noise and that zero becomes small, making the rank or PCA cutoff a scale-aware modeling decision. An SVD routine should return dimensions and status, not just three arrays. Check <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> </math> relative to a declared input scale; check <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>U</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>U</mi> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>V</mi> </math> separately, with identity sizes matching full/thin conventions; verify descending nonnegative singular values; enforce a maximum iteration count and surface nonconvergence. Passing these checks establishes those measured properties at the tested scale; it does not certify every singular value or guarantee an accurate solution for an ill-conditioned application. Phase 7 - The moving-panel tracebook Use active right-handed rotations, column vectors, radians in code, and the declared illustrative minus-Z projection with near 1, far 10 and NDC depth <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math>. One local point reaches a screen-relative description Let local scale be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, orientation a positive-Z quarter turn, translation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, and point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. The camera sits at world <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> with identity orientation. Stage Value Check Scale local point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Scaling occurs in the declared local axes. Rotate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Right-hand positive Z maps X toward Y. Translate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> World location; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>M</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>T</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mi>S</mi> </math>. Inverse camera pose <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Camera is five units above the world plane and looks along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo>−</mo> <mi>Z</mi> </math>. Projection to clip <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>35</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>9</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Keep all four homogeneous coordinates. Perspective divide <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>5</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>7</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>9</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Finite nonzero divisor; this point is within the selected clip volume. Reconstructing local coordinates undoes translation, then rotation, then scale. Applying the inverse orientation with a guessed untranslated offset would mix frames. The same row-major scalar array could implement every operation if logical access and upload conventions remain correct. The tangent and normal take different paths Take local tangent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>u</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and local normal <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Scale then rotate gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>u</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Reciprocal-scale then rotate gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>n</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Their dot is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math>. Normalizing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>n</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> </math> for shading changes its length, not the perpendicularity. Neither vector receives translation. A mirrored model additionally needs an explicit winding/orientation policy. Diagnose interpolation using a quarter point Interpolate identity to a positive-Z <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>120</mn> <mo>∘</mo> </msup> </math> orientation. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>t</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>4</mn> </math>, ideal SLERP gives a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>30</mn> <mo>∘</mo> </msup> </math> turn. NLERP normalizes coefficients <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>7</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>8</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <msqrt> <mn>3</mn> </msqrt> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>8</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, yielding about <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>27.795772496</mn> <mo>∘</mo> </msup> </math>. The midpoint alone would not expose this speed difference. With endpoints <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo>−</mo> <mi>q</mi> </math>, sign-aligning first avoids a zero midpoint and preserves the common orientation. A parent edit invalidates only actual dependencies For car → door → mirror, editing the door’s local transform makes door-local and door-world caches stale, along with mirror-world and derived inverse/normal caches. Mirror-local and car caches remain valid. Reparenting the mirror changes its world dependency even if its local coefficients remain identical. Preserving world pose during reparenting instead requires solving the new local map and checking whether the result still fits the allowed TRS representation. Phase 6 - The robot panel tracebook This cumulative trace extends the self-contained Phase 6 volume. The numbers are illustrative laboratory inputs, not observations from a real robot or renderer. One physical object through six representations Start with metre-valued workcell points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>C</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and sensor point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>P</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Column 1: Stage Column 2: Intermediate value Column 3: Meaning and check Edge subtraction Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>e</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>e</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Meaning and check Point differences, not new point locations. Dot and Gram Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>g</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mn>11</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>16</mn> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>g</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mn>12</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>g</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mn>22</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>9</mn> </math> Meaning and check Perpendicular but non-unit edge basis. Cross Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>e</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>×</mo> <msub> <mi>e</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>12</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Meaning and check Oriented area vector in square metres. Normalization Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> Meaning and check Finite unit front normal; triangle area is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>6</mn> </math>. Sensor coordinates Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>β</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>4</mn> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>γ</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>α</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>12</mn> </math> Meaning and check Sum is one and all weights are positive. Attribute interpolation Intermediate value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>12</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>20</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>40</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>50</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>35</mn> </math> Meaning and check Affine temperature model, not an asserted physical heat solution. Move a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> above the panel. The area normal dotted with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mi>A</mi> </math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>24</mn> </math>, yielding tetrahedron volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>4</mn> </math>. Swap <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>C</mi> </math> and both signs reverse; ordinary area and volume do not. A mirror changes orientation, not all measurements Mirror horizontal coordinates with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>R</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>diag</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. New first edge is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and second edge remains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Their cross becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>12</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. All edge lengths and all original pairwise dot products remain unchanged. The Gram matrix cannot tell us that the orientation flipped. What the executed lab actually demonstrates The inline scalar program checks the panel weights, area, frame, projection, rejection, reflection, finite-state rejection, huge/tiny scaled normalization, angles, transmission and total internal reflection. None of these tests certify all floating-point inputs, performance, a robust orientation implementation, or human understanding. Frame history can be clean and wrong Follow a moving character:
The previous frame sees the character at a pixel. The character moves, exposing the background. Incorrect reprojection brings the old character color into that background. Accumulation reduces random noise but retains a ghost.
A depth or identity mismatch can justify rejecting that history. A gaze-region change creates a second problem. An old peripheral sample may belong to the correct surface but lack the detail required now. Lower MSE or lower variance alone does not establish that the reused information is correct. An allocation claim and a runtime claim are different Normalize the original frame time to one: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi data-mjx-auto-op="false">old</mi> </mrow> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.6</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mn>0.4</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1.</mn> </math> Only the second component benefits. If its work becomes 70% cheaper: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi data-mjx-auto-op="false">new</mi> </mrow> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.6</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mn>0.4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.72</mn> <mo>.</mo> </math> The speedup is: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mi>S</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>0.72</mn> </mfrac> <mo>≈</mo> <mn>1.3889</mn> <mo>.</mo> </math> The calculation assumes additive, non-overlapping costs. A real GPU may have overlap, bandwidth limits, occupancy changes, or synchronization costs. A post-filtered full reference does not establish that any original shading work was skipped. Assignment failure versus successful ownership transfer Start A with byte7 and B with byte9 in separate buffers. Prepare B=A with an injected allocation failure: B still holds byte9 at the same live buffer, A still byte7, and allocation count is unchanged. Move-construct C from A: C owns byte7, A is documented empty. Copy-construct from empty A: new owner is empty without traversing a null range. Move-assign C into B: B’s byte9 allocation is released, B takes byte7, C becomes empty. Self-move B through its alias preserves its value under this particular owner’s contract. Reset B to empty and end scope: live allocation count0. The aliased update does not behave like two copies For destination+=source; source*=0.5, starting with distinct source4/destination4 gives destination8/source2. If both parameters designate one float, its state is4→8→4. The second statement sees the first statement’s write. Passing scalar values instead creates independent parameter values; no caller mutation is implied. The immovable same-type prvalue result remained valid in both. This differentiates language-required direct construction from a compiler-selected named-local elision. A trace should include a concrete input, every state transition that matters, the final output, one invariant check, and one deliberately failing or boundary input when useful. M001 - The 0xAD control byte Introduced by: C001 / M001 Input and conventions Schema, from least to most significant position: bits 0-2 mode | bit 3 visible | bits 4-5 quality | bit 6 locked | bit 7 dirty Input: {mode=5, visible=1, quality=2, locked=0, dirty=1}. Field zero occupies the least-significant available bits. State-by-state trace mode 5 << 0 = 00000101 visible 1 << 3 = 00001000 quality 2 << 4 = 00100000 locked 0 << 6 = 00000000 dirty 1 << 7 = 10000000 OR result 10101101 = 0xAD Base interpretations: binary 10101101 = 128 + 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = decimal 173 hex 1010 1101 = A D = 0xAD octal 010 101 101 = 2 5 5 = 0255 Quality extraction: 10101101 >> 4 = 00001010 00001010 & 03 = 00000010 = 2 LSB-first bit-array packing of [1,0,1,1,0,1,0,1] accumulates 01, 05, 0D, 2D, then AD; unpacking index 5 computes (0xAD >> 5) & 1 = 1. Result and invariant checks
Every field round-trips to its input value. The five fields occupy eight non-overlapping bits exactly. Changing quality to 3 clears 0x30, writes 0x30, and yields 0xBD; all non-quality bits remain unchanged.
Boundary or failure trace OR-only replacement fails when a new value needs to clear an old 1. For example, replacing quality 3 with 1 via word | (1 << 4) leaves the old high field bit set and still decodes as 3. Clear-before-OR produces the intended 1. M002 - Carry and overflow are different questions Introduced by: C002 / M002 Input and conventions Use eight-bit result storage. C is the ninth unsigned bit, V reports signed two’s-complement range failure, N copies result bit 7, and Z tests whether the low result byte is zero. State-by-state trace Case 1 - signed overflow without carry: 01111111 unsigned 127, signed 127 + 00000001 unsigned 1, signed 1 ---------- 10000000 unsigned 128, signed -128
C=0: no ninth bit; unsigned 128 fits V=1: signed mathematical 128 does not fit [-128,127] N=1: result high bit is set Z=0: result is nonzero Case 2 - carry without signed overflow: 11111111 unsigned 255, signed -1 + 00000001 unsigned 1, signed 1 ---------- 1 00000000
C=1: unsigned mathematical 256 needs a ninth bit V=0: signed mathematical result is valid zero N=0: low result high bit is clear Z=1: low result byte is zero Subtraction example: 13 - 5 = 13 + (~5 + 1) 00001101 + 11111011 = 1 00001000 -> low byte 8 Result and invariant checks
C and V are independent; neither can replace the other. N reports the stored sign bit, not whether a signed overflow occurred. An eight-bit emulator must retain a wider temporary long enough to compute C, then mask the architectural result.
Boundary or failure trace 10000000 represents -128. Complement-plus-one returns 10000000 because mathematical +128 cannot fit. At the fixed-bit residue level the pattern is stable; evaluating same-type signed negation in C++ overflows and is undefined. Reconstructing each state change Decimal to binary and back For 173, successive quotient/remainder pairs are (86,1), (43,0), (21,1), (10,1), (5,0), (2,1), (1,0), (0,1). The remainders are low bits first, so reverse them to get 10101101. Horner accumulators while reading this result are 1,2,5,10,21,43,86,173. This checks both directions without assuming that the displayed order equals array order. Replacing a field while preserving neighbors Replace quality 2 with 1 in AD: field width w=2, offset s=4 low mask L=03; positioned mask M=30 eight-bit NOT(M)=CF clear: AD & CF = 8D encode new value: (01 & 03) << 4 = 10 write: 8D | 10 = 9D read back: (9D >> 4) & 03 = 01 outside field: AD & CF = 9D & CF = 8D The last equality proves preservation rather than only checking the new field value. Multiplication by selected partial products Multiply 13 by 11. Start result=0, partial=13, multiplier=11. A low multiplier bit of 1 includes the partial product; shift the multiplier right and the widened partial left between stages. Column 1: Stage Column 2: Multiplier Column 3: Low bit Column 4: Partial Column 5: Result after inclusion 0 Multiplier 1011 Low bit 1 Partial 13 Result after inclusion 13 1 Multiplier 0101 Low bit 1 Partial 26 Result after inclusion 39 2 Multiplier 0010 Low bit 0 Partial 52 Result after inclusion 39 3 Multiplier 0001 Low bit 1 Partial 104 Result after inclusion 143 Check 13×11=143. The widened partial is essential: if it were retained in a narrow original operand, shifts could lose bits before the accumulator sees them. Division by shifting the remainder Divide binary 1101 (13) by 3, reading dividend bits from most to least significant. At each stage append the next bit to the partial remainder, compare with 3, subtract if possible, and append the quotient decision. Column 1: Incoming bit Column 2: Remainder before compare Column 3: Subtract 3? Column 4: New remainder Column 5: Quotient prefix 1 Remainder before compare 1 Subtract 3? no New remainder 1 Quotient prefix 0 1 Remainder before compare 3 Subtract 3? yes New remainder 0 Quotient prefix 01 0 Remainder before compare 0 Subtract 3? no New remainder 0 Quotient prefix 010 1 Remainder before compare 1 Subtract 3? no New remainder 1 Quotient prefix 0100 Quotient 4 and remainder 1 satisfy 13=4×3+1, with 0≤1<3. C++ expression types and a safe index For uint8_t a=250,b=10 on the host used here:
Stored operands are eight-bit unsigned values. Integral promotion converts each to int because int represents 0–255. Addition executes as int arithmetic, producing int 260. auto keeps int 260; explicit conversion to uint8_t stores residue 4.
For int index=−1 and unsigned size=10, an ordinary mixed-sign comparison may convert −1 to a large unsigned value. std::cmp_less(-1,10u) correctly returns true mathematically, but that alone does not authorize indexing. The valid condition is index>=0 && std::cmp_less(index,size). Binary subtraction and incoming borrow Take A=5, B=3. With carry C=1, compute 5+NOT₈(3)+1=5+252+1=258: result=2, carry-out=1 (no borrow). With C=0, compute 257: result=1, since an incoming borrow subtracts one extra. For A=3,B=5,C=1, exact unsigned difference is −2: low result=254, carry-out=0 (borrow). This is the binary SBC convention, independent of any repository implementation claim. M003 - Bytes to physical memory A matching and mismatching endian decode Offset LE byte BE byte LE reader accumulator after byte 0 78 12 00000078 1 56 34 00005678 2 34 56 00345678 3 12 78 12345678 Bytes are hexadecimal. Reading LE bytes as BE produces 78563412; no intra-octet bit reversal occurs. A schema version=1, count=0x12345678, payloadSize=9, written U8/U32-LE/U64-LE, yields: 01 78 56 34 12 09 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 Field offsets are 0/1/5, length 13. A typical native record places fields at 0/4/8, size 16. Packing may resemble the schema length but does not define its byte order or version contract. Struct layout and an aligned array Assume member size/alignment pairs 1/1, 8/8, 2/2, 4/4. Column 1: Member Column 2: Previous end Column 3: Aligned start Column 4: Occupied offsets Column 5: New end flags Previous end 0 Aligned start 0 Occupied offsets 0 New end 1 id Previous end 1 Aligned start 8 Occupied offsets 8-15 New end 16 layer Previous end 16 Aligned start 16 Occupied offsets 16-17 New end 18 color Previous end 18 Aligned start 20 Occupied offsets 20-23 New end 24 Holes are seven plus two bytes; payload 15, size 24. Reordering id/color/layer/flags gives 0-7/8-11/12-13/14 plus one tail byte: size 16. Verify on the target ABI. A 1/4/1 record ends at nine but has size 12. At base 0x1000, next object starts 0x100C and its integer at 0x1010. A fictitious stride nine would put that integer at 0x100D, breaking alignment. Page translation with an unchanged offset Assume 4-KiB pages and an allowed resident mapping. VA 0x12345ABC P 0x1000 = 4096 VPN = VA / P 0x12345 offset = VA % P 0xABC mapping VPN 0x12345 -> PFN 0x987 frame start 0x987000 PA = start + offset 0x987ABC Process B may map the same VPN to another PFN; adjacent virtual pages may map distant frames. These are address-space mappings, not endian conversions. Four bytes starting at offset FFE occupy FFE/FFF in page one and 000/001 in page two. A valid first mapping does not prove the second readable. Four bytes at cache-line offset 62 similarly span two 64-byte lines. One member load, separated by mechanism Assume active at offset zero, IEEE-754 32-bit float at offset four, object VA 0x12345000, valid alignment, and 4-KiB pages.
Member offset produces VA 0x12345004. Split into VPN 0x12345 and offset 004. TLB/page-table lookup supplies allowed PFN 0x5A7. PA=0x5A7004; cache/memory supplies bytes. With stated little-endian float representation, 00 00 80 3F corresponds to bits 3F800000 and float 1.0; IEEE-754 floating point develops why later.
A TLB miss can walk valid tables without OS faulting. A nonresident valid page can fault, acquire backing, and resume. A forbidden access may fail. Real processors overlap this conceptual sequence. Ownership and lifetime, not geography A local vector object commonly occupies a frame; elements occupy its separate dynamic buffer. A copied span points to elements, not vector metadata. Returning that span after destroying the vector dangles it; reallocation can also invalidate views. Keeping an owner alive is necessary but not always sufficient. Static locals retain storage across calls; automatic const locals need not use read-only mappings; string literals have static storage and must not be modified. Old numeric addresses or remaining bytes do not extend lifetime. Fault recovery and copy-on-write Two mappings share frame F read-only. For a permitted private COW write, OS allocates F2, copies F, changes the writer’s mapping to F2 with write permission, and restarts. Not every protection violation is repairable. Diagnosis: absurd decoded value→byte order; second array element misaligned→stride/tail padding; released vector span→lifetime; first-touch latency→fault/commitment; allocation fails amid holes→fragmentation; published file lost after crash→publication versus durability. Three failure paths that must not be confused
A code outside0–15 fails the nibble contract before packing. A huge claimed shape fails checked size arithmetic/resource policy before allocation. A same-size changed payload can pass structure checks while failing an independent integrity comparison.

This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Standard-layout and trivial copyability — Standard-layout and trivial copyability Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C007 · Latest development: C009 Definition and mechanism Rule-Zero composition is not itself a trivially-copyable, standard-layout or serialization promise. Hand-written/defaulted special functions can change triviality, and relocation is not generic permission to memmove a nontrivial owner. Standard-layout is a structural language property supporting useful low-level layout reasoning; it does not promise no padding or a portable ABI. Trivial copyability permits particular byte-copy operations on valid objects/representations, not arbitrary byte validity or serialization. Aggregate, trivial and trivially-copyable are separate traits. Prerequisites
ABI and object layout — ABI offsets and padding must be separated from standard-layout and byte-copy language eligibility.
Used by Later chunks extend this same node; dependent concepts are listed here as they are integrated. Recall and next depth Give an example, explain why the rule exists, and identify which guarantee would be missing if the prerequisite were ignored.
